label: shuffleArray.loop
reason: Shuffle iterations directly determine CPU work; the call site now passes ~10% more iterations, so per-call latency will increase proportionally (and this function is called once per movie during graph initialization).

label: randomWalkWithRestart.init_and_shuffle_graph
reason: Initialization loop walks every node, does seedMovies.includes(movie) and shuffles each adjacency list; the increased shuffle iterations amplify total upfront CPU time proportional to graph size.

label: orama_hybrid_search
reason: Search limit increased (1000→1100), which likely increases hybrid search work (scoring, vector retrieval via includeVectors) and response materialization; this is typically the dominant latency component.
return_value_change: searchMovies can return a larger and/or different set of hits (and thus different ordering after reranking) because the upstream Orama search now requests 1100 results instead of 1000.

label: search_postprocess_and_levenshtein_rerank
reason: With a higher hit limit, downstream work grows: mapping hits to candidates, Levenshtein-based ordering, and map/filter steps are all O(hits) or worse; this can become significant as hits increase.
return_value_change: Because more hits are processed into candidates and reranked, the returned list may include more items and/or different items/order than before, potentially impacting callers that assume a stable cap or ordering.

label: rateLimiter.consume
reason: Mongo-backed rateLimiter.consume(req.url) can incur database/network latency on every request; measuring it provides baseline and helps contextualize downstream error-path overhead.

label: rateLimiter.errorLogging
reason: New console.debug("rateLimiter.consume failed", e) in a request middleware error path can add synchronous/IO overhead and expensive error object formatting/serialization, especially if rate-limit rejections are frequent.
